18.t: Working with data: eDNA versus netting
q: Calculate the percentage of all species found that were detected by eDNA.
Explain how eDNA can detect species that netting misses.
Fish shed cells, mucus and faeces into the water; tiny amounts of their DNA are amplified by PCR and matched to a database, so rare or hidden species are detected without catching them.
One species was found only by netting. Suggest two reasons.
Any two: its DNA was not in the samples taken (patchy distribution); the DNA had broken down; the primers did not match its sequence; it is missing from the reference database.
Evaluate eDNA as a replacement for netting.

For: more species, far less fieldwork, no harm to fish. Against: it cannot count, measure or age fish, and cannot show whether DNA came from a living fish in the lake. Best used together with netting.
eDNA was found for a fish not seen in the lake for 20 years. Suggest two explanations other than the fish being present.
DNA washed in from upstream or carried by birds; contamination of the sample; old DNA preserved in mud.
